Combined speed bin distributions for single-unit short-haul vehicles Sadly, for refuse trucks, no additional categories can be removed from their cautionary classification due to aggregation across hours. The shaded graphs only have between 3 and 13 vehicles. For urban roads on weekdays, there are now 31 and 39 vehicles and 558 and 3,293 hours of recorded data for freeways and other roads, respectively. These distributions can be utilized to update MOVES. We again see a peak at 60 mph on freeways and 5 mph on other roads. Weekend distributions do look relatively similar but are lacking solid vehicle counts; weekday and weekend data could be combined and applied to weekends to get an approximation of refuse behavior, which may be an improvement over current non-source-specific MOVES defaults. The data aggregated over day types and hour IDs are saved to the file speedDistributionResults_byRoad_source.csv, which includes distributions for refuse trucks and all other source types as well, and look very similar to the following weekday graphs. We recommend incorporating urban weekday distributions into MOVES as-is and using the data irrespective of day type, as given in the file above for urban weekend refuse truck speed distributions. 55 This report is available at no cost from the National Laboratory of the Rockies (NLR) at www.nlr.gov/publications. Figure 44. Combined speed bin distributions for refuse trucks For transit bus data, we also lack robust vehicle counts traveling on weekends. On weekends, we observed 17 and 21 buses driving on freeways and other roads, respectively, but we do have 82 and 352 respective recorded hours. Despite the low vehicle counts, data come from several unique fleets across the country, and there are many recorded hours, so these distributions could be incorporated into MOVES with prudence. We see similar behavior between weekends and weekdays with a peak at 60 mph on freeways, albeit a wider peak on weekdays when there are more data at 26 vehicles and 617 logged hours, and a broad, smooth peak surrounding 10 mph on other roads. 56 This report is available at no cost from the National Laboratory of the Rockies (NLR) at www.nlr.gov/publications.
